questions.prompt: A compromised identity is actively deleting data and the incident owner authorizes containment. Which rule is sound?

options.label: Contain active harm promptly and record the continuity tradeoff.
Never disable a shared identity under any circumstances.
Wait for complete certainty about every consumer before stopping harm.

questions.explanation: Urgent authorized containment can interrupt legitimate workloads. Neither an absolute never-disable rule nor an unbounded dependency search justifies allowing known active destruction.

questions.prompt: A log names Account R used by several builds. What does that identify?

options.label: Only the account’s creator can use it.
The acting principal; identifying the human or workload requires more evidence.

questions.explanation: Shared keys and impersonation can involve multiple consumers. The principal identifies an access identity, while actor attribution needs issuance, workload and audit evidence.

questions.prompt: A persistent key is deleted, but a worker already holds a short-lived token. What is established?

options.label: That key route changed; the issued token needs a separate validity and access check.
All issued tokens necessarily stopped immediately.

questions.explanation: Credential deletion and already-issued token validity are distinct boundaries. Neither instant invalidation nor indefinite authorization follows without the applicable token and permission evidence.

questions.prompt: Build A succeeds after recovery; Release B has not run. What is the accurate receipt?

options.label: Build A is verified; Release B remains unverified.
Build A success proves containment failed.

questions.explanation: Verify each consumer independently. One working operation establishes neither the other consumer’s recovery nor the old credential’s continued validity; those have separate checks.

questions.prompt: A repository search finds no use of the key. What can be concluded?

options.label: The secret is safe to commit as documentation.
No use was found within the searched scope; external consumers remain unknown.

questions.explanation: A scoped search cannot enumerate every external secret store or consumer. Credential values remain outside documentation even when no references appear in the inspected repository.
